purpose: Catch irreversible macro placement, channel, power, and pin-access decisions that later placement/CTS/routing cannot economically undo without a full re-floorplan.

checks.question: Do hard-macro edges leave channels wide enough for the expected bus + clock + power traffic, or are there knife-edge corridors?
checks.evidence_demanded: Floorplan view with channel-width annotations and estimated track demand per channel; congestion estimate from a quick global-route trial.
checks.red_flag: Any channel narrower than ~2× the widest expected bus plus power straps, or a trial route already showing overflow in the corridor.
checks.why_it_matters: Later placement will jam cells into the bottleneck; congestion and detours become permanent and force timing or DRC failures that only a macro move can fix.

checks.question: Are power-grid straps and via arrays pre-placed with density that matches the expected current density of each region?
checks.evidence_demanded: Power-plan overlay showing strap pitch, width, and via-farm locations versus early power-budget numbers.
checks.red_flag: Large logic regions with no intermediate straps or via arrays under high-power blocks.
checks.why_it_matters: IR and EM problems discovered after placement require ripping up routes and often the placement itself.

checks.question: Do block-level pin placements align with the top-level bus plan so that abutment or short routes are possible?
checks.evidence_demanded: Pin-to-pin flylines or early global-route of the top-level nets; abutment check if hierarchical.
checks.red_flag: Major buses that must cross the entire die or that land on the opposite side of a macro from their destination.
checks.why_it_matters: Forces long top-level routes that steal tracks from the blocks and create unfixable timing paths.

checks.question: Is the clock spine / H-tree reservation present and clear of macros that would force later CTS detours?
checks.evidence_demanded: Clock-plan layer showing reserved tracks or regions; macro keep-out relative to the planned spine.
checks.red_flag: Macros sitting directly on the intended clock spine with no alternate path of comparable length.
checks.why_it_matters: CTS will either produce huge skew or consume signal-routing resources trying to go around.

checks.question: Have keep-out, blockage, and soft-placement guides been set so that high-fanout or timing-critical logic is not forced into dead zones?
checks.evidence_demanded: Blockage and guide map; list of known critical clocks or interfaces and their intended regions.
checks.red_flag: Critical interface logic with no legal placement region near its pins.
checks.why_it_matters: Placement will push critical cells far away; pre-CTS timing will look hopeless and force late floorplan changes.

checks.question: Is the die size / utilization target realistic given macro area + estimated standard-cell area + routing overhead for the node?
checks.evidence_demanded: Area report: macro area, estimated std-cell area, utilization target, and routing-track budget for the technology.
checks.red_flag: Utilization already >75-80% (older nodes) or >65-70% (advanced nodes with complex design rules) before any placement.
checks.why_it_matters: Placement will either fail to legalize or produce unroutable density; the only fix is a larger die or fewer features.

checks.question: Are IO and power pads placed with correct package and ESD constraints, and do the related feed-throughs have clear paths?
checks.evidence_demanded: Pad ring view, package ball map, and early feed-through plan.
checks.red_flag: Power pads clustered far from high-current blocks or signal pads whose feed-throughs cross the densest logic.
checks.why_it_matters: Package-level IR and signal integrity problems appear only at signoff and require pad or floorplan changes.

kill_questions: Show me the trial global-route congestion map on this floorplan—are there any regions already red before a single standard cell is placed?
If I move this largest macro 50 µm, does any major bus or clock spine become unroutable?
waiver_culture: Narrow channels and optimistic utilization are frequently waived under schedule pressure; the cost is almost always a mid-project floorplan revision or a permanent frequency/area hit once routing and IR numbers come in.

purpose: Confirm that placement has produced a legal, density-healthy, and roughly timing-feasible starting point so that CTS does not inherit unfixable skew or congestion problems.

checks.question: Is the placement legal and density-controlled, with no residual overlaps or hotspots above the node’s practical limit?
checks.evidence_demanded: Density map, legalization report, and hotspot list; peak density numbers by region.
checks.red_flag: Any region still above ~70-80% (node-dependent) after legalization, or cells left unplaced.
checks.why_it_matters: CTS and routing will fight the same hotspots; buffer insertion will only make density worse.

checks.question: Show the pre-CTS setup slack histogram by clock group—where is the wall and how long is the negative tail?
checks.evidence_demanded: Slack histogram or cumulative distribution per clock; WNS/TNS numbers with idealized clocks.
checks.red_flag: Wall sitting at −200 ps or worse, or a long tail of paths more negative than a few buffer delays.
checks.why_it_matters: CTS can only redistribute existing path delay; deeply negative paths will remain failing and force placement ECOs after clock insertion.

checks.question: Are the high-fanout nets (resets, scans, enables) already buffered or explicitly marked for CTS/HFNS treatment?
checks.evidence_demanded: Fanout report for non-clock nets above a threshold (e.g., 30-50); list of nets still unbuffered.
checks.red_flag: Large unbuffered high-fanout nets that will become timing or transition killers once real parasitics appear.
checks.why_it_matters: CTS tools often ignore or poorly handle non-clock HFNs; they become post-CTS surprises.

checks.question: Do the placement of clock-gating cells and integrated clock gates sit near the center of their fanout cones?
checks.evidence_demanded: Clock-gate placement overlay versus sink locations; latency estimate from gate to sinks.
checks.red_flag: ICGs placed at the edge of a large cone or clustered in one corner of the die.
checks.why_it_matters: CTS will build long, unbalanced branches from those ICGs, creating skew that is hard to recover.

checks.question: Is scan-chain order and placement compatible with the functional placement, or will scan reordering create long routes?
checks.evidence_demanded: Scan-chain length and displacement report; visual of a few long chains.
checks.red_flag: Large average or maximum scan displacement that will add congestion or hold problems later.
checks.why_it_matters: Post-CTS scan fixes are expensive and often re-break timing.

checks.question: Have all dont-touch, size-only, and path-group constraints been applied so that the placement did not optimize away critical structure?
checks.evidence_demanded: Constraint audit report and a sample of critical-path cells showing they kept their intended sizes/locations.
checks.red_flag: Critical cells that were resized or moved contrary to explicit constraints.
checks.why_it_matters: CTS and later optimization will start from a corrupted baseline; the original intent is lost.

checks.question: Is the congestion map after placement still acceptable for the subsequent clock and signal routes?
checks.evidence_demanded: Global-route congestion map with placement frozen; overflow numbers by region.
checks.red_flag: New red spots that appeared only after placement, especially near macros or in narrow channels.
checks.why_it_matters: Clock routes will consume the remaining tracks; signal routing will fail or detour badly.

kill_questions: Show the pre-CTS slack histogram— if the wall is not near zero, why are we inserting clocks instead of fixing placement?
Are there still unbuffered high-fanout non-clock nets above the threshold we agreed?
waiver_culture: Mild negative pre-CTS tails and residual density hotspots are often waived with 'CTS will fix it'; the later cost is extra clock buffers, higher power, and a longer post-CTS timing convergence loop.

purpose: Confirm that all corners, modes, and exception strategies produce a timing picture that will still be true after the final mask changes and that no hidden optimism remains.

checks.question: Across every setup corner and mode, is WNS ≥ 0 (or within the agreed signoff margin) and is TNS bounded, with no exploding path count?
checks.evidence_demanded: Full corner/mode timing summary table; WNS/TNS and failing-endpoint counts.
checks.red_flag: Any signoff corner still negative beyond the documented margin, or TNS that grew after the last ECO.
checks.why_it_matters: A single missed corner is a silicon failure; late discovery forces a respin or a frequency bin split.

checks.question: Are hold corners clean after the final hold-buffer ECO, and did those buffers re-break setup in any related corner?
checks.evidence_demanded: Hold summary per corner; setup-vs-hold delta report on the paths that received hold buffers.
checks.red_flag: New setup failures that appeared only after hold fixing, or hold still failing in the min corners.
checks.why_it_matters: Hold ECOs are often done late; undetected setup re-breaks become silicon escapes.

checks.question: Show the slack histogram for the most critical clock groups— is the wall cleanly at or above zero with no long negative tail?
checks.evidence_demanded: Per-clock-group slack histograms at the signoff corners.
checks.red_flag: A tail of paths still >50-100 ps negative while the bulk is clean (indicates residual hard paths or missing exceptions).
checks.why_it_matters: Those tail paths are the ones that fail on the tester or in the field under noise.

checks.question: Have all false-path, multicycle, and set_max_delay exceptions been reviewed for correctness and is the list frozen?
checks.evidence_demanded: Exception audit report (who added, why, evidence); sample of the most powerful exceptions with protocol justification.
checks.red_flag: New or undocumented exceptions added in the last week, or exceptions whose justification is only 'it was failing'.
checks.why_it_matters: An incorrect false-path is a functional silicon bug; an overly tight max_delay wastes area but is safer than a missing one.

checks.question: Is clock uncertainty / derate / AOCV consistent with the final CTS latency and the foundry technology file for this node?
checks.evidence_demanded: Uncertainty and derate table versus CTS report and foundry application notes; comparison of applied vs recommended values.
checks.red_flag: Uncertainty numbers that were never updated after final CTS, or AOCV tables from a different node.
checks.why_it_matters: Optimistic derates produce optimistic timing that disappears on silicon; pessimistic ones hide the true critical paths.

checks.question: Do the timing reports include the final extracted parasitics (or the agreed signoff extraction corner) and not an intermediate SPEF?
checks.evidence_demanded: Extraction header and timestamp in the timing run; comparison of a few critical net capacitances against the extraction log.
checks.red_flag: Timing still running on an older or idealized parasitic file.
checks.why_it_matters: The difference between intermediate and final extraction is often exactly the margin that was left.

checks.question: Are there any remaining unconstrained or partially constrained endpoints (especially I/Os and asynchronous interfaces)?
checks.evidence_demanded: Unconstrained-endpoint report and check_timing summary.
checks.red_flag: Any sequential endpoint or port that is not covered by a clock or a max/min delay.
checks.why_it_matters: Unconstrained paths are invisible to STA and become field failures when exercised.

checks.question: Has noise / SI analysis been run on the final routes and have the aggressor updates been reflected in the timing windows?
checks.evidence_demanded: SI summary and delta-timing report before/after noise; list of nets that changed slack significantly.
checks.red_flag: Large SI-induced slack degradation that was never fixed or waived with data.
checks.why_it_matters: On advanced nodes SI can move timing by tens to hundreds of ps; ignoring it is a common escape.

kill_questions: Show the full corner/mode WNS table— is every signoff cell green, and if not, where is the written waiver with silicon risk assessment?
Walk me through the three most powerful false-path or multicycle exceptions and the protocol evidence that justifies them.
waiver_culture: Small residual negative tails and a handful of SI or hold violations are frequently waived with 'margin exists in silicon'; the cost is occasional speed-path fallout, extra guard-banding on the next revision, or a quiet frequency reduction after tapeout.

purpose: Guarantee that the final GDS is manufacturable and matches the schematic, catching geometry, connectivity, and reliability problems that no timing or placement review can see.

checks.question: Is the DRC clean at the foundry-signoff rule deck and deck revision, or are the remaining violations only the explicitly waived set?
checks.evidence_demanded: Final DRC run summary with rule-deck version, error count by type, and the waiver list with owners.
checks.red_flag: Any non-waived error, or waivers that lack a foundry-approved justification or layout screenshot.
checks.why_it_matters: Unclean DRC is a direct mask or yield risk; late discovery forces a respin.

checks.question: Does LVS report zero discrepancies (or only the documented intentional ones) against the final netlist used for timing?
checks.evidence_demanded: LVS summary, discrepancy list, and cross-check that the netlist timestamp matches the timing signoff netlist.
checks.red_flag: Any unexplained device or net mismatch, or a netlist that is not the one that timed clean.
checks.why_it_matters: LVS mismatches are functional bugs or missing cells that timing never saw.

checks.question: Are antenna violations cleaned or diode-protected, and is the antenna ratio report within foundry limits for every layer?
checks.evidence_demanded: Antenna report by layer and node; list of remaining diodes or jumpers added.
checks.red_flag: Any antenna error above the foundry limit without a protection cell or metal jump.
checks.why_it_matters: Antenna damage is a yield and reliability killer that appears only after fabrication.

checks.question: Has ERC (electrical rule check) been run for floating gates, missing ties, well/substrate connectivity, and ESD paths?
checks.evidence_demanded: ERC summary and the list of remaining warnings with disposition.
checks.red_flag: Floating gates, unconnected wells, or ESD paths that do not reach the pads.
checks.why_it_matters: These become leakage, latch-up, or ESD failures in the package.

checks.question: Are density and metal-fill rules satisfied for every layer, including the final fill inserted after the last ECO?
checks.evidence_demanded: Density maps per layer and fill-log timestamp relative to the last layout change.
checks.red_flag: Density windows out of range or fill that was never re-run after late ECOs.
checks.why_it_matters: Density violations cause CMP problems and yield loss; fill that overlaps late ECOs creates new DRC.

checks.question: Do the via and contact arrays meet the foundry’s minimum-cut and enclosure rules, especially under high-current power nets?
checks.evidence_demanded: Via-enclosure and cut-count checks; EM-critical net list with via counts.
checks.red_flag: Single-cut vias on EM-critical nets or enclosure violations on fine layers (more severe at advanced nodes).
checks.why_it_matters: Via reliability failures appear as early life or field returns.

checks.question: Has the final GDS been compared (XOR or layer-diff) against the previous frozen version so that only intended ECOs appear?
checks.evidence_demanded: GDS diff report and the ECO list that explains every difference.
checks.red_flag: Unexpected geometry changes outside the ECO list.
checks.why_it_matters: Unintended edits are a classic source of last-minute LVS/DRC or functional breaks.

checks.question: Are all IP blocks (memories, analog, PHYs) present at the correct revision and LVS-clean against their own abstract or CDL?
checks.evidence_demanded: IP version manifest and per-block LVS black-box or grey-box results.
checks.red_flag: Any IP at a different revision from the one that was timing- and integration-validated.
checks.why_it_matters: Wrong IP revision is a functional or yield mismatch that is extremely expensive to discover after tapeout.

kill_questions: Is the DRC/LVS run log using the exact foundry signoff deck and the exact netlist that timed clean—show the version strings?
Are there any open antenna, density, or ERC errors that do not have a written, foundry-aligned waiver?
waiver_culture: Minor density and antenna waivers are common and usually accepted by the foundry with documentation; what later hurts is waiving LVS discrepancies or via-enclosure issues that turn into yield or reliability problems once the part is in volume.
